messages:
Sam R: FYI — customer reported their embeddings index failing after we finished a pinned-model rollout yesterday. They say their app started returning a vector length error on inserts.
Priya K: Which customer / stack? can you paste the error and a sample request?
Sam R: Customer: AtlasSearch (third-party). Running our embeddings endpoint -> then writes to a managed index that expects 1536 dims. Error from their index service: `Vector length mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024`
Sam R: Quick repro payload they used:```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX
{
  "model": "open-embed-family/auto",
  "input": ["what is the refund policy?"],
  "batch_size": 1
}
```
Sam R: Response snippet:```json
{
  "data": [{"embedding": [0.0012, 0.023, ..., 0.999]}],
  "model": "open-embed-family-v2",
  "model_vector_size": 1024
}
```
Sam R: They had pinned to `open-embed-family` (alias) months ago and expected the 1536 variant. Looks like the alias resolved to a new v2 (1024) during the rollout.
Priya K: Oof. Can you confirm the pinned model was an alias and not a concrete version id? pinned-by-customer vs pinned-by-infra?
Sam R: From their support dashboard: they used `model_alias: open-embed-family` in their config (not a specific variant id). They thought alias would be stable.
Tomas G: Quick take from infra: last night's canary pushed `open-embed-family-v2` as the new default for that alias. We intended to keep backward-compat, but v2 changed architecture => vector size reduced to 1024. Alias mapping change triggered sends to v2 for any non-versioned requests.
Tomas G: Root cause = alias-to-variant mapping update + customer relying on alias for pinned behavior. Also our pinning UI allowed selecting "alias" which we incorrectly treat as stable.
Priya K: Repro steps for support/debugging (useful to share with customer):
1) Re-run the curl with explicit model id (if available) to confirm vector size. e.g. `model: open-embed-family-v1-1536`
2) If the response shows `model_vector_size: 1024` then the selected model is v2.
3) Indexer error will be identical: `Vector length mismatch`.
4) As temporary workaround, request embeddings with explicit older variant or run a reindex job to migrate vectors to new size.
Sam R: Customer asked for an immediate mitigation — they can't reindex millions of docs right away. Any quick compatibility options?
Tomas G: Short-term options:
- Serve new requests through a compatibility shim that pads/truncates client-side? (dangerous for semantics)
- Route their embeddings to a pinned dedicated pool running the old v1 weight (we still have snapshots) — requires we host v1 for them (cost).
- Provide a per-customer alias override to force alias -> v1 mapping for 48-72h while they plan reindex.
Priya K: I can propose the per-customer alias override as a stopgap. Need eng approval for config change and to ensure no cross-customer impact. @Tomas G can you confirm feasibility and how long to put that in?
Tomas G: Feasible. Small config flag in routing table. I can deploy a hotfix to add `customer_alias_overrides` and set `open-embed-family -> open-embed-family-v1-1536` for AtlasSearch. Risk is low if scoped to one account. ETA ~2-3 hours (manual deploy + smoke).
support-bot: deploy triggered by @Tomas G: `deploy/alias-override-hotfix` — status: queued
DevOps: Heads-up, we should validate autoscaler behavior when pinning v1 for a single tenant — might need an extra GPU in the pool if traffic spikes.
QA Automation: I'll run a quick regression: make sure alias overrides don't leak across tenants. test cases: alias override, default alias, explicit version id.
Priya K: Messaging plan for customer:
- Apologize for the regression.
- Offer temporary alias override while they plan reindex (include ETA).
- Document recommended path: reindex to v2 when ready or explicitly pin to v1 variant in their infra.
Sam R: Customer replied asking "why did the alias change?" They want explanation for governance + assurances.
Tomas G: We'll own the mistake: the alias rollout had a missed note in the release that v2 changes vector size and is not backwards compatible. We should add a check to block alias promotion if vector_size != previous_vector_size for that alias family, or require a breaking-change flag and customer opt-in.
Priya K: Action items:
- Tomas: deploy alias override for AtlasSearch now (assign + ETA).
- Tomas + DevOps: ensure capacity for v1 pinned traffic.
- Engineering: add guardrail to alias promotion pipeline (blocking PR).
- Support (Priya/Sam): send mitigation + timeline to customer and offer a migration plan doc.
Tomas G: Deployed override for AtlasSearch -> confirmed routing to `open-embed-family-v1-1536`. Smoke test: ran embed call -> response `model_vector_size: 1536` and customer index accept succeeded.
Sam R: Customer confirmed interim fix works, thanks. They asked for long-term docs on pinning semantics.
Priya K: I'll draft a KB: "Pinned models, aliases, and compatibility" — include: always pin exact variant for embeddings, how to detect model_vector_size in responses, reindex guidance, and contact channels for override requests.
Sam R: Adding note for product: change UI to make alias vs concrete version selection explicit with compatibility warning. @Tomas G can we add a modal on alias selection?
Tomas G: Yep, filing a small product/UX ticket.
QA Automation: Tests added to regression suite to catch alias->variant incompatible promotions.
Sam R: Closing loop: customer satisfied with temporary workaround and roadmap. Keeping thread open until guardrail is in prod. :thumbsup:
